decisive_moments.reason: Pro directly conceded the strongest limitations of standards, then reframed the comparison around long-term ecosystem adaptability and explained how versioning, conformance, provenance, and permissions can mitigate—not eliminate—those limitations.

Pro made the prototype-versus-production distinction explicit and connected standards to switching costs, auditability, competition, and adaptation across model generations, addressing the rubric's long-term and developer-freedom dimensions.

Con correctly identified unresolved problems—semantic incompatibility, integration security, accountability, and the possibility that vertical integration improves outcomes—but largely asserted that these outweigh contestability without comparative evidence.

flags.quote: portability and competition reduce cost and expose failures
A vertically integrated system can therefore provide users greater reliability and protection at lower total cost
